info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package pubsub is your message bus: publish, subscribe, and durable streams your apps read at their own pace.

post.summary: Publish puts one message on the org's bus.
post.description:
Publish puts one message on the org's bus. When a stream captures the subject
the write is DURABLE — the receipt names the stream and sequence only after
JetStream has it on storage, and a repeated Nats-Msg-Id header within the
dedup window answers duplicate instead of storing twice. When nothing
captures it, the message goes out core NATS: delivered to current
subscribers, receipt {ok}, nothing retained.

post.summary: Request sends one request on the org's bus and waits for one reply — the synchronous half of pub/sub, for callers speaking to a responder subscribed on the NATS port.
post.description:
Request sends one request on the org's bus and waits for one reply — the
synchronous half of pub/sub, for callers speaking to a responder subscribed
on the NATS port. 404 when nobody is listening on the subject; 408 when a
responder exists but no reply arrived within the timeout.

duplicate.description:
Duplicate is true when JetStream deduplicated the message by its
Nats-Msg-Id instead of storing it again.

ok.description: OK is true when the bus accepted the message.

seq.description: Seq is the message's sequence in that stream.

stream.description:
Stream is the stream that stored the message — absent when no stream
captures the subject and the message went out core (fire-and-forget).

data.description: Data is the payload as UTF-8 text.

headers.description: Headers are the message's headers, when it carries any.

seq.description: Seq is the message's stream sequence — fetched messages only.

subject.description: Subject is the message's subject in the org's own namespace.

time.description:
Time is when the stream stored the message, RFC3339 — fetched messages
only.

data.description:
Data is the payload, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).
Binary payloads belong on the NATS port.

headers.description:
Headers are optional message headers, one value per name. A Nats-Msg-Id
header is JetStream's deduplication key: a repeat within the stream's
dedup window is acknowledged as duplicate rather than stored twice.

subject.description:
Subject is the subject to publish to, in the org's own namespace — e.g.
orders.created. No wildcards.

data.description: Data is the request payload, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text.

headers.description: Headers are optional request headers, one value per name.

subject.description: Subject is the subject a responder listens on, in the org's namespace.

timeoutMs.description:
TimeoutMs bounds the wait for a reply. 0 or less means the default of
5000; anything above 30000 is clamped to 30000.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
